title: Tag Helpers
description: Enhance standard HTML elements with server-side behavior using ASP.NET Core tag helpers.

blocks.text: Tag helpers are server-side components that enhance standard HTML elements with additional attributes. They let you generate correct URLs, bind form fields to model properties, and apply validation without writing C# code inside your HTML.

Unlike HTML helpers, which use method calls inside @ expressions, tag helpers look like plain HTML. They are easier to read and edit, especially for designers who are more comfortable with markup than C# syntax.

blocks.title: Tag Helpers Are Server-Side
blocks.text: Tag helpers run on the server before the page is sent to the browser. The browser never sees the asp- attributes; it only receives standard HTML.

Tag helpers are enabled by default in new ASP.NET Core projects. The _ViewImports.cshtml file contains a single line that activates all built-in tag helpers from the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.TagHelpers assembly.

blocks.title: ViewImports Configuration
blocks.content: Enable tag helpers for all views in a folder.

blocks.text: ASP.NET Core includes tag helpers for the most common web development tasks. The anchor tag helper generates correct URLs, the form tag helper adds antiforgery tokens and action attributes, and the input and validation tag helpers bind fields and display errors.

blocks.title: Built-in Tag Helpers
items: <a asp-controller asp-action> - Generates a link with the correct URL and route values.
<form asp-controller asp-action> - Generates a form tag with the correct action URL and an antiforgery token.
<input asp-for> - Binds an input to a model property and adds validation attributes.
<select asp-for> - Binds a dropdown to a model property from a list of options.
<textarea asp-for> - Binds a multiline text area to a string property.
<span asp-validation-for> - Renders a validation error message for a property.
<div asp-validation-summary> - Renders a summary of all validation errors.

blocks.title: A Form Using Tag Helpers
blocks.content: Tag helpers replace HTML helpers with cleaner markup.

blocks.text: The rendered HTML includes the correct action URL, a hidden antiforgery token, id and name attributes bound to the model property, and data-val attributes for client-side validation. You get all of this without writing a single line of C# in the view.

The anchor tag helper is one of the most frequently used tag helpers. It generates the href attribute based on the controller, action, route values, and area. If the link points to the current page, it adds class="nav-link" automatically in some templates.

blocks.title: Generating Links with Anchor Tag Helper
blocks.code: View @product.Name View Laptop

blocks.text: When built-in tag helpers are not enough, you can create your own. A custom tag helper is a C# class that inherits from TagHelper and overrides the Process or ProcessAsync method. You can target a specific HTML element, add or replace attributes, and modify the content.

blocks.title: A Bold Tag Helper
blocks.content: Wrap text in a strong element automatically.

blocks.title: Custom Tag Helpers Are Advanced
blocks.text: Custom tag helpers are powerful but require a solid understanding of the tag helper pipeline. Start with built-in tag helpers before writing your own.

terms.definition: A server-side component that enhances HTML elements with ASP.NET Core behavior using attributes.
A tag helper that generates correct hyperlinks based on controller, action, and route values.
A tag helper that generates a form tag with the correct action URL and an antiforgery token.
A tag helper that binds an input element to a model property and adds validation attributes.
A developer-created tag helper class that modifies HTML elements with custom server-side logic.

blocks.title: Exercise: Convert HTML Helpers to Tag Helpers
blocks.description: Refactor a Razor view to use tag helpers instead of HTML helpers.
steps: Create a LoginViewModel with Email and Password properties.
Create a Login Razor Page with a POST handler.
Replace Html.BeginForm with a <form asp-controller asp-action> tag helper.
Replace Html.LabelFor and Html.EditorFor with <label asp-for> and <input asp-for>.
Add <span asp-validation-for> and <div asp-validation-summary> for errors.
Run the page and verify the rendered HTML contains the correct attributes and antiforgery token.
blocks.expectedOutcome: The view will use tag helper syntax that is cleaner and easier to read than HTML helper method calls.

items.text: I know how to enable tag helpers in a project.
I can use asp-for to bind an input to a model property.
items.hint: <input asp-for="Email" /> binds to the Email property.

items.text: I can generate a link using asp-controller and asp-action.
I understand why tag helpers are generally preferred over HTML helpers.
items.hint: They look like standard HTML and are easier to read and edit.

blocks.title: Summary
points: Tag helpers enhance HTML elements with server-side behavior using asp- attributes.
They are enabled by default via _ViewImports.cshtml.
The anchor, form, input, select, and validation tag helpers cover most scenarios.
Custom tag helpers can be created by inheriting from TagHelper.
Tag helpers keep markup readable by looking like plain HTML.
blocks.takeaway: Tag helpers are the bridge between clean HTML markup and the powerful server-side features of ASP.NET Core. They make views easier to write and easier to maintain.
